title: Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)
description: Update static pages after they’ve been built without redeploying. The best of both worlds!

slides.title: Static but Up‑to‑Date 🔄
slides.content:
# The Problem

SSG is fast but the data can become stale until you rebuild.

SSR is fresh but slower and more expensive.

**ISR** gives you the speed of static with the freshness of server‑side. 🥇

You enable it by adding the `revalidate` key to the return of `getStaticProps`.

slides.title: ISR in Action (pages/posts.js)
slides.content: Set `revalidate: 60` to regenerate the page at most once every 60 seconds.

quizData.question: If `revalidate: 10`, how often will the page be regenerated?

options.text: At most once every 10 seconds when a request comes in

quizData.explanation: ISR regenerates the page in the background when a request arrives and the cached page is older than `revalidate` seconds. It's not a constant rebuild.

slides.title: On‑Demand ISR (Stable Since v12.2) 🎉
On‑Demand Revalidation API (pages/api/revalidate.js)
slides.content: Secure this with a secret token so only your CMS can trigger it.

quizData.question: Which scenario is best for ISR?

options.text: A static blog that never changes
A product listing page that updates a few times per day

quizData.explanation: ISR shines for pages that are mostly static but occasionally need updates, like product catalogs or blog indexes.
